title: SpecRunnerRunClosure
description: The closure record of one spec-runner invocation (`runs/<run_id>/closure.json`, #480 FR-07): the last record of a run, written once by the dispatcher's `finally` however the handler left. The `closure_kind` vocabulary is pinned here and derived mechanically by `closure.derive` from how the handler left and whether work was left undone -- no exit site chooses it. A run-start with no closure is read as crash/unknown, never as an empty success.

pipeline_id.description: Pipeline id of the invocation, when one was set.

closure_kind.description: How the invocation ended. completed: exit 0 and nothing left undone. refused: non-zero exit and the last unsuccessful attempt's error_kind is a rule's refusal (policy, budget, blocked, hook_failure, harness_guard). failed: any other non-zero exit, or exit 0 with unfinished work. interrupted: a signal or KeyboardInterrupt. crashed: an unhandled exception.

reason.description: Free text for a human. Not a vocabulary, not validated, may be empty.

exit_code.description: The exit code of the process. Distinguishes 1 (the work was bad) from 2 (the instrument could not tell), both `failed`.

last_checkpoint_id.description: Id of the last acknowledged checkpoint, or null.

last_call_ids.description: call_id of every paid call this invocation started, in order.

attempt_ids.description: `<task_id>-<n>` of every attempt this invocation recorded. Empty together with no calls reads as 'there was nothing to do'.

open_calls.description: Calls with an acknowledged start and no recorded result at exit.

degraded.description: True when the run continued on a degraded record (spool).
